correctness.rationale: The action on the degree 6q Jacobian-ring residue is the monomial weight plus the determinant weight 15, so invariance means weight 3 modulo 6. Direct enumeration in review-evidence/checks.py (argument 3) gave primitive counts (0,70,290,70,0); the hyperplane square adds one invariant and rational coarse cohomology is the invariant part. The projective eigenspace intersections for powers 1 and 5 are empty. For each of powers 2 and 4 the three two-coordinate eigenspaces give 18 points, paired freely by the residual involution; the four normal weights give age 2. Power 3 has two plane sextics; the residual order-three action is free, making each quotient genus 4, and the three negative normal eigenvalues give age 3/2. These exhaust the sectors. In the specified unshifted-sign convention the Euler values are 435 and 441. The packaged computation was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The quotient is motivated, but the claimed fractional refinement adds no new sector geometry: the prior local quotient types, genera and counts make the fractional and point terms automatic. The only new input is a single standard degree-six character projection. Grouping the six weights by the order 1,2,3,6 of the evaluating root gives coefficient counts 426,10,3,1, so h31=(426−10+2·3−2·1)/6=70; h22 then follows from Euler 435. Thus the residual delta is a routine, mechanically evaluable application of the residue character rule to an already classified example. The record does not identify a mathematical need for that residual split beyond the routine completion of the polynomial, nor derive any new pattern, obstruction or distinction from it. This is a value decision, not a claim that the polynomial is incorrect or previously printed.
